turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1]. Is [PERSON_2] joining us?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: He's here, he's just in the other room finishing up a call with one of the branches. He'll pop on in a sec.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: No rush. How is Charlotte? I saw you guys got hammered with rain last week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Oh, it was a mess. We had, I want to say, three days straight. Which, honestly, for us is not the worst thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Water heaters, sump pumps, the phones were ringing off the hook.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Right, one person's bad week is a great week for plumbing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Exactly. Our dispatch team was not thrilled with me when I said that out loud, though.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, sorry, sorry, I'm here. The Gastonia branch had a van break down, so that was fun.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_2]. No worries at all. Everything okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, yeah, we got it towed, we moved two jobs to the Belmont crew. Just a Tuesday. Well, a Wednesday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Ha. Okay, so I put an agenda in the invite, but it's pretty loose. I wanted to go through the Q3 numbers, talk about where you're at with Signal AI and the summaries rollout, and then, since we're about twelve weeks out from renewal, just get a sense of how you're both feeling going into that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Does that work?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That works. I have a hard stop at eleven, just so you know.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Totally. Quick numbers, let me pull it up. Okay. So Q3, you had about forty-one thousand inbound calls across the fourteen branches, which is up eleven percent over Q2.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Paid search is still your biggest source, a little over half. And the booked-job rate on paid search calls was thirty-eight percent, which is actually your best quarter since you came on.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Is that across all fourteen, or is Belmont skewing it again?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Let me look. Um, Belmont is high, they're at forty-four percent, but even if you take them out you're at thirty-seven.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: The one that's lagging is Matthews, they're at twenty-nine, and that's mostly because their after-hours calls go to the answering service and a lot of those don't convert until the next morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, Matthews is the one branch we still roll to the answering service after six. We keep talking about bringing that in-house.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: If you do, it's a small change on our side. We'd just update the call flow so after-hours calls for Matthews ring your central dispatch line instead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Takes a few minutes.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, good to know. I'll talk to [PERSON_4] about it, she'd have to staff it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And then Meta is still small for you, right around six percent of calls, but the booked rate there is decent, thirty-one percent.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So not nothing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, we're testing more on Meta in Q1. We'll see. Our agency wants to push it, I'm a little skeptical.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: But anyway, overall, that is good to hear, because it does not feel like our best quarter.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Tell me more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So this is the thing I really wanted to get into today. The calls are coming in, the bookings are fine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: But on the Google Ads side, the offline conversions are showing up two, sometimes three days after the call. And it's not every now and then, it's been most of September and October.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Two to three days from when the call happens to when it shows up as a conversion in Google Ads?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. And so what happens is Smart Bidding

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sorry, can I, just so [PERSON_3] has the full picture. It's the booked job signal specifically, right? Not the call itself?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, the booked job one, that's the one we bid on. Anyway, so Smart Bidding sees a day where we spent, whatever, nine grand and got barely any conversions, and it panics and pulls back.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And then three days later all the conversions land and it goes, oh, never mind, and swings the other way. So we're basically bidding on last week's data.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. Okay. Yeah, that would make the account look really choppy.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Choppy is a nice word for it. Our CPA in Google went from about eighty-five dollars to a hundred and twenty in like five weeks, and my CMO keeps asking me why.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And I don't have a good answer for him other than the conversions are late.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Did anything change on your side around then? New conversion actions, the GCLID capture, anything with the tag on the site?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not that I know of. [PERSON_2], did Priyanka change anything?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No, she checked. The conversion actions are the same ones from last year. Nothing changed on our end.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. I'll open a ticket with our integrations team today, and I'll ask them to pull the upload logs for your account so we can see when we're sending versus when Google is accepting them.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I've heard something similar from at least one other customer this month, so I want to see if it's the same thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Please. Because I'll be honest with you, this is the one that keeps me up at night.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And the other piece, [PERSON_3], I'll just say it. CallRail's been emailing me, like, every week. Their rep keeps telling me they push conversions to Google same day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I don't know if that's true, I haven't looked into it, but it's hard to ignore when we're sitting here three days behind.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah. That's fair, and I appreciate you telling me. I'd want to see what same day actually means for them, there's usually some fine print.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: But that's not a reason for us to be three days late. Understood.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah. I'm not shopping. I'm just saying the emails are getting harder to delete.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Ha, fair enough. Okay, let's talk Signal AI, because I know you've been living in there, [PERSON_2].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, so, mostly good. The one thing, and I sent Priyanka down a rabbit hole on this, Signal AI is tagging a lot of our after-hours calls as spam, and they're not spam.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: They're people with a burst pipe at eleven at night. They're booking jobs.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Huh. How many are we talking about?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So we pulled forty of the after-hours calls it marked as spam last week and actually listened to them, and thirty-one were real customers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Real jobs. A couple of them were four-hundred-dollar emergency calls.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thirty-one out of forty. Okay, that's a lot.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It is. And the problem is the spam ones drop out of the reporting, so the after-hours campaign looks terrible, and then somebody says, hey, why are we paying for after-hours ads.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Which is me. I'm the somebody.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: She's the somebody.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Is it overnight calls specifically, or anything outside business hours?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It seems like it's mostly after about nine p.m., and weekends. Short calls, people who are kind of panicked and just give their address and hang up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Those seem to get flagged. But that's me guessing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: No, that's helpful. My guess is the spam model is leaning on call length, and maybe on the time of day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll send this over to the Signal AI team with your examples if you can share the call IDs.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll send you the spreadsheet. Priyanka has it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. And the summaries, how is that going? You turned those on for dispatch in, what, August?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Oh, the summaries. Honestly, the dispatchers love them. Like, genuinely. [PERSON_4] told me they used to have to listen to the first minute of every call to figure out what the person even wanted, and now they just read the summary and go.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's great. That's really good to hear.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It probably saves each of them an hour a day, I'd guess. She'd say more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: She would say two hours. She exaggerates.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll take an hour. Um, and the branch managers, are they reading them too, or is it just dispatch?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Mostly dispatch for now. A couple of the managers check them when there's a complaint, but we haven't really pushed it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, that's maybe something we look at next quarter. Oh, and [PERSON_2], how was the trade show? You were in Orlando, right?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Orlando, yeah. It was fine. A lot of booths, a lot of software people. No offense.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: None taken. I am a software people.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Ha. Honestly the best part was a panel on technician retention. Everybody's got the same problem, nobody wants to crawl under a house in August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Can't imagine why.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Ha. Okay, so [PERSON_1], you mentioned renewal. I know we're still a few months out, but I'd rather hear it now than in December.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah. So a couple of things. Our finance team, [PERSON_5] specifically, has been going through all of our software renewals for next year, and he asked me why PreSense is an add-on at all. His words were, it feels like paying twice.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Because we're already paying for the calls and the call data, and then PreSense is this separate line item on top.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And I tried to explain it. Like, no, PreSense is the part that passes what they were looking at on the site to the agent before they pick up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And he said, okay, but isn't that just the call data? And I didn't love my answer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah. I can put together a one-pager for [PERSON_5] on what PreSense is doing for you specifically. We can look at the booked rate on calls where the agent had the page context versus calls where they didn't.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That would help. He's a numbers guy. If it's not a number, it doesn't exist.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. I can do numbers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And then, I guess, the bigger thing. I don't want this to sound like a threat, because it's not. We like you guys.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: But if the Google piece isn't fixed by renewal, we'll have to look around. I don't want to, but I'd have to, because I can't go to my CMO and say, yeah, we're renewing the thing that's making our CPA worse.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: No, that's completely fair, and I'd rather you tell me straight. I'll make sure the integrations ticket gets the right priority, and I'll give you an update by the end of next week either way, even if the update is that we're still digging.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay. I appreciate that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, that'd help.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Anything else on your list? I think you had something about adding users.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Oh, yeah, small thing. We're opening the two new branches in January, Rock Hill and Concord, so we'll need tracking numbers and a couple more seats.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll send you Priyanka's list.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Easy. I'll get the numbers provisioned once I have the list. Okay, so on my side: the integrations ticket on the offline conversion delay goes in today, with the upload logs.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: The after-hours spam examples go to the Signal AI team once [PERSON_2] sends the call IDs. A one-pager on PreSense for [PERSON_5].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And the new branch numbers in January.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Last thing, I promise. Are you guys doing anything for Thanksgiving?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: My in-laws are coming. So, pray for me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: We're doing the Panthers game. Well, my son is making me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Ha. Good luck with that. Okay, thanks, both of you. I'll send notes this afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks, man.
